newsitem.title: USA: Laboratory Corp sees recapitalization need.
newsitem.headline: Laboratory Corp sees recapitalization need.

text.p: Laboratory Corp of America Holdings says it will need to recapitalize to meet any settlement payments in connection with an industry-wide investigation by the government.
The company said only that the probe involves "past laboratory marketing practices at a number of laboratories."
Laboratory Corp said it took a third quarter charge of $185 million to create reserves to cover anticipated government and private claims resulting from the investigation.
The charge was included in a third quarter loss of $1.19 per share the company reported Thursday.
The company said it has obtained a waiver to exclude the charge from covenant calculations of a recently amended credit agreement.
Laboratory Corp operates primary testing facilities and performs medical diagnostic tests. It has estimated annualized revenues of $1.6 billion.
Laboratory Corp shares closed Thursday at 3-1/4, near its year low of 3-1/8.

"While LabCorp cannot be assured of a successful recapitalization, it believes that both public and private sources of funds may be available to it to complete such a program by March 31, 1997," the company said in a release.
If a recapitalization plan is not in place by the required time, the company said it will require additional waivers or amendments.

The company said in the second quarter it needed a recapitalization plan based on company performance, and potential settlement costs would enhance a need for recapitalization, said company spokeswoman Pamela Sherry.
